Spoken popup native source reconstruction

This is maintained binary source material, not a display/acceptance report.
The executable images are the configured Steam and official Windows PE files.
No game process, window, translator, or translation check executes here.

Full source ownership
---------------------
native-role-correspondence.tsv pairs every one of the 42 complete ELF
decompiled source owners with its current decoded PE source. It retains the
ELF C path, both PE ranges and both original instruction bodies. The literal
co-reference evidence is in reference-source-mapping.tsv and its classic
counterpart. Small leaf text formatters with no PE unwind entry are located
through decoded calls in the actual dispatcher and source owners; their
entries are not silently discarded for lacking unwind metadata.

The complete native topic dispatcher has selectors 0..253. The Steam owner
is 0x1404988b0..0x1404df174; its main 254-entry switch dispatch is 0x14049a050,
table 0x1404de19c. reference-topic-dispatch.tsv and classic-topic-dispatch.tsv
retain all slots, shared target aliases, and upstream enum labels. The labels
come from local df-structures; targets and branches come from executable bytes.
Additional dispatcher switches, remap bytes, conditional edges and fallback
branches remain in the corresponding switches/branches/instruction sources.

The speech wrapper is Steam 0x140684a10..0x1406858fc and official
0x140682430..0x14068331c. It is the same complete production for every topic,
rather than a prefix inferred from the screenshot. Its ELF C source is
elf-speech-wrapper.c. The complete 42-owner C reconstruction remains available
as elf-<role>.c. The full PE inventory contains decoded instructions and manual
source productions; the focused current-PE Ghidra C exports for the
mental-picture formatter and element supplier are listed in the final section.

Normalized wrapper production (storage/allocation mechanics are omitted;
all native branches remain in its full source bodies):

  speaker = find_unit(speaker_ref.unit_id);
  if (speaker exists) {
      if (adventure_mode)
          header = full_speaker_caption(speaker, relative_to_player,
                                        article/capitalization/name_flags);
      else if (native anonymous/identity conditions hold)
          header = anonymous_unit_caption(speaker);
      else
          header = whole_unit_name(speaker);
  } else if (speaker_ref.historical_figure resolves) {
      header = language_name(historical_figure.name);
  } else {
      header = "";
  }

  if (adventure_mode && speaker_is_player)
      header = "You";
  if (header != "" && recipient_is_player)
      addressed_player_flag = true;
  else if (header != "" && recipient_ref.unit_id != -1) {
      if (recipient unit resolves)
          header += " (to " + native_recipient_caption(recipient) + ")";
      else
          addressed_player_flag = false;     // no invented recipient text
  }

  body = speech_parameter_expansion(body, speaker_ref, typed_parameters);
  capitalize_initial(body);
  if (header != "") header += ": ";        // native literal 0x1406852ce
  if (speaker exists && race/caste indices are valid
      && caste_flags contains the native speech-transform bit)
      body = native_speech_transform(body);
  complete_report = header + body;
  retain_speech_record(original_ref, topic, typed_parameters, flags);
  if (native visibility/distance/routing admits the speech)
      submit_announcement(complete_report, native_report_type);

Silent or open branches are explicit: no unit/historical speaker produces no
header or colon; unavailable recipient produces no (to ...) header; invalid
race/caste uses the original body; native visibility/distance can retain the
speech record while omitting report submission. Complete wrapper sources retain
the extra "stops and pays attention to you." announcement and type/category
routing, so these do not become fabricated speech sentences.

Speech transform is Steam 0x14067b6c0..0x14067bc4d, called at wrapper
0x140685380. It replaces S/s through temporary ([LIP])/([lip]) markers, then
expands them into native repetitions. Both markers, every search/replace loop,
random repetition bound and punctuation behavior are retained in
reference-speech-transform.asm and classic-speech-transform.asm. They are
temporary construction controls, not additional dialogue topics or names.

Incident/memory source
----------------------
The refusal-to-identify body originates in incident type 10; this reconstruction
includes the complete type 0..10 source, not only the refusal branch.
Steam source: 0x14066ba00..0x14066fe48.
Official source: 0x140669420..0x14066d868.
Complete previous C: elf-dialogue-1016060.c (ELF 0x1016060..0x101b7e6).
The main native selector is incident+4 with unsigned bound 10. A null incident
returns immediately; out-of-range types return without appending text.

  switch (incident.type) {
    0 DEATH:
      corpse-found memory -> "I found myself dead." or
        "I found " + ("you" | incident_person(victim)) + " dead.";
      speaker is the victim -> "I died.";
      otherwise -> ("You" | initial_capital(incident_person(victim)))
        + " " + death_cause_clause + ".";
      death_cause dispatch includes every numeric alias 0..54 and its default;
      cause 53 adds gender-selected himself/herself/itself when HF resolves;
      missing HF leaves the native shorter drowned branch.

    1 CRIME:
      absent memory or memory subtype != 0 -> no text;
      otherwise -> ("You" | initial_capital(incident_person(actor)))
        + (" attempted " | " perpetrated ") + native_crime_clause + ".";
      crime lookup/default and all 0..18 crime switch arms are retained.

    2 ATTACK:
      ("You" | initial_capital(incident_person(actor))) + " attacked "
        + ("you" | incident_person(victim)) + ".";

    3 ESCALATION:
      ("You" | initial_capital(incident_person(actor)))
        + " escalated a conflict with "
        + ("you" | incident_person(victim)) + ".";

    4 REUNION:
      native participant/knowledge choice yields "I was reunited with ",
      "You were reunited with ", or capitalized incident person +
      " was reunited with "; facilitator adds " due to your efforts" or
      " and it is all thanks to " + incident_person(facilitator).
      Full participant/self/facilitator alternatives are in the complete C.

    5 YIELD_DEMAND:
      ("You" | initial_capital(incident_person(actor)))
        + " demanded submission from "
        + ("you" | incident_person(victim)) + ".";

    6 PERFORMANCE:
      participant/observer/not-witnessed modes remain distinct;
      subtypes 0..4 are story, poem, music, dance and sermon;
      stored form, written-content, history-event and participant role fields
      determine the title and the story/recite/play/sing/chant/speak/dance/
      preach verbs; no participants has its native passive/anonymous wording.
      Speaker participation, viewer participation, multiple music performers,
      invalid form/role and untitled-work fallback are separate branches.
      Titles are whole language_name or stored authored content, not literals.
      Location appends " at " + abstract-building-name when its id is present;
      a supplier returning empty preserves the native final "at ." production.

    7 ARTIFACT_LOCATION:
      states 0..4 emit had/placed/obtained/gave/would not give respectively;
      state 5 emits artifact-name + " was destroyed";
      states 3 AND 4 append " to " + ("you" | incident_person(receiver));
      then native site/building/region/underground location branches run.

    8 WRITTEN_CONTENT_LOCATION:
      states 0..1 emit placed/gave; state 1 appends receiver;
      written-content title or "an untitled work" is followed by the same
      native site/building/region/underground location construction.

    9 GAVE_IDENTIFICATION:
      no identifier -> "Somebody named themself";
      first identifier is viewer -> "You named yourself";
      otherwise -> initial_capital(incident_person(first_identifier))
        + " self-identified";
      all append " to " + entity_name(incident.entity) + ".".

    10 REFUSED_TO_IDENTIFY:
      no refuser -> "Somebody refused to name themself";
      first refuser is viewer -> "You refused to name yourself";
      otherwise -> initial_capital(incident_person(first_refuser))
        + " refused to give a name";
      all append " to " + entity_name(incident.entity) + ".".
  }

The exact case-10 terminal blocks are Steam 0x14066edc1 (You), 0x14066edd5
(incident person), 0x14066ee64 (Somebody), all reaching 0x14066ebb5 (" to "),
0x14066ebd5 (entity-name), then the shared period path. The second slot is an
entity/civilization identity, not an incident_person merely because its current
proper name resembles a person's name. Invalid entity yields the finite
"an unknown civilization"; a valid entity with empty generated name supplies
the empty string and therefore produces the complete native "to ." sentence.

The previously missed state-4 receiver is proved in the current Steam image:
0x14066c6e9 reads artifact state; 0x14066c6eb subtracts 3; zero reaches
0x14066c6f4; 0x14066c6f0 compares the remaining value to 1; state 4 also reaches
0x14066c6f4 (" to "). Receiver uses 0x140c1d100 for viewer identity or
0x140b92af0 for the full incident person, through 0x14066c761 common location.
Official source retains the same branch at addresses offset by -0x25e0.

Typed dynamic suppliers
-----------------------
incident_person: Steam 0x140b92af0..0x140b92f0c; handles true/visual/historical
HF identity, witness identity ids, I/me/my/myself and unknown creature. It calls
historical-reference 0x140b92f10, unit-reference 0x140c3a590 and creature/caste
description 0x140b94ed0. These suppliers retain zombie/ghostly/corpse/name/role,
unidentified creature, unknown creature, pronoun and ownership alternatives.
speaker_caption: wrapper calls Steam 0x141330c30, with full sender name,
profession/creature description and dead/corpse alternatives. No arbitrary
English proper-name inventory can replace these typed generated fields.
entity_name: Steam 0x140b92900..0x140b92a78; entity lookup, optional ENT page
markup, language_name at entity+0x20, and unknown-civilization fallback.
language_name: Steam 0x140a946e0..0x140a94ea2; first name/nickname and generated
language-word forms; these remain open fields with their authored component.
location: site b93930, abstract building b94090, region b94940 and underground
b94a40; all use actual id/name suppliers. Underground additionally has fixed
world-deeps/magma-sea/underworld clauses and silent/empty name branches.
performance: form and written-content lookups, history_event virtual text,
sermon value/sphere/name and title fields; recursive event text follows its
existing full source catalog rather than a made-up finite name list.

Markup [LPAGE:HF:...], [LPAGE:ENT:...], [LPAGE:SITE:...], [/LPAGE] and parameter
tokens belong to native field construction. Their grammar/control alternatives
are retained; numeric ids and user-authored names stay opaque field content.
Literal whitespace is normalized only for the translation productions; raw
instructions and native literal operands preserve the original source bytes.

Catalog connection
-------------------
The finite body/source productions belong to the existing complete
announcement spoken corpus and the actual runtime data files
announcement-dialogue-grammar.tsv, announcement-dialogue-extra-grammar.tsv,
announcement-description-grammar.tsv and announcement-reference-grammar.tsv.
The 42-owner full decompiled source and native topic/call inventories describe
the popup's body universe; announcement-popup-native retains submission,
report storage, alert routing and complete report-text renderer ownership.
The new current-PE material establishes branch and supplier provenance for
these catalogs, including finite silent/empty supplier branches. It does not
claim that arbitrary generated names, authored content or RAW descriptions
form a finite list of all possible complete strings.

Mental-picture speech in the adventure announcement popup
---------------------------------------------------------
The speech "The prophet <speaker>: <historical figure> is displeased."
is an additional source path through this SAME popup. It is the mental-picture
formatter, not the visitor overview renderer, and its source is not limited to
the DISPLEASURE adjective visible in the supplied image.

The current Windows Steam and official images were actually decompiled with
Ghidra 12.1.4, using their decoded function bounds and native jump-table
destinations. These C files are direct Ghidra output rather than a manual
semantic reconstruction or compiled project code:

  reference-dialogue-1014100.c     0x140659090..0x14065a250
  classic-dialogue-1014100.c       0x140656ab0..0x140657c70
  reference-mental-picture-element.c  0x140658e20..0x14065908a
  classic-mental-picture-element.c    0x140656840..0x140656aaa

Their image identities remain PE:6a70a6d9:02711000 and
PE:6a70b91c:0270a000 respectively. Ghidra's "Switch is manually overridden"
annotation records explicit switch destinations supplied from the actual PE
jump-table bytes. The six-action and 170-entry emotion destinations are also
preserved individually in reference-switches.tsv and classic-switches.tsv.
The main formatter's code ends at Steam ret 0x140659f8c / official ret
0x1406579ac; the remaining unwind extent includes its native embedded tables.
The element decompilation retains UNK references for tiny shared pronoun
literals; their exact address/text mappings are preserved in
../visitor-overview/<edition>-prophet-quote-subject-helper-literals.tsv.

Direct spoken dispatch, topic 220 ShoutBeliefStoryFrame:

  Steam case entry 0x1404cd82a, body call 0x1404cd8e8,
        capitalization 0x1404cd91f, speech wrapper call 0x1404cd97c.
  Official case entry 0x1404cb3ea, body call 0x1404cb4a8,
        capitalization 0x1404cb4df, speech wrapper call 0x1404cb53c.

  body = "";
  belief = find_belief_by_id(talk_choice.field_0x58);
  if (belief != null) {
      story = belief.stories[talk_choice.field_0x5c];
      picture = story.frames[talk_choice.field_0x60];
      body = format_picture(picture, speaker_context, listener_context);
  }
  if (body.empty()) body = "I don't remember what I believe...";
  capitalize_initial(body);
  spoken_announcement(speaker_context, listener_context, body, ...);

The two story/frame indices are selected stored fields in this topic. This
case contains no random selection; the helper's visitor-overview caller and
the greeting supplier are separate callers. The direct topic's speaker and
listener contexts are forwarded unchanged, so I/me and you remain possible,
in addition to actual historical-figure, site and world names. Its final
speaker/profession header uses the complete shared wrapper described above.

The greeting supplier also calls the same formatter at Steam 0x14067f872 /
official 0x14067d292. It selects a belief story/frame, appends nonempty output
to its existing greeting using the native double-space separator, and follows
its other native greeting branches when no picture text was produced. The
complete supplier is reference-dialogue-1048a40.asm and its official/ELF
counterparts. Consequently the mental-picture grammar must be reachable for
both an entire speech body and a sentence embedded in a longer speech body.

Complete bounded formatter productions
--------------------------------------
The semantic reconstruction in ../visitor-overview/decompiled-grammar.txt
describes the SAME formatter and element helper, including all native field
offsets, subject suppliers, temporal flags and silent/default paths. The
current PE C above independently retains those same branches. Its full scope:

  * First TIME property (type 8), first ACTION property (type 1); ACTION wins
    over EMOTION even if its actor is -1 and therefore returns empty.
  * Six ACTION values: APPEAR, DESTROY, SPOKE, BURN, FLOOD and REWARD, with
    base / third-person / past / continuous forms. Unknown action values
    preserve the already-assembled subject, copula, object and period.
  * Continuous / non-continuous and no TIME / TIME flags 0, 1, 2 or both;
    first / second / third person. Both TIME bits retain the source's exact
    concatenation and precedence rather than an inferred corrected tense.
  * Optional indexed target with role 1 (object), plus "to " for SPOKE.
    Missing target (-1), unnamed elements and unknown element types retain
    native whitespace/punctuation behavior rather than inventing a name.
  * First EMOTION property (type 3) when no ACTION exists, with the same
    complete subject and person suppliers, past/future/present copulas and
    final period. A missing emotion element (-1) returns empty.
  * All 170 EMOTION selectors for values -1..168: 130 different emitted
    strings, 40 aliases of the empty adjective branch, plus out-of-range
    default. -1 emits "emotionless"; DISPLEASURE is value 45 and emits
    "displeased" (Steam case 0x140659a53 -> literal 0x1416634e8;
    official case 0x140657473 -> literal 0x14165e388).
  * No ACTION/EMOTION returns empty; other picture-property kinds do not
    produce text. Direct topic 220 then uses its remembered-belief fallback.

The indexed emotion rows are now retained for BOTH Windows editions in
../visitor-overview/reference-prophet-emotion-branches.tsv and its classic
counterpart. All six verb families and object separators are already in
../visitor-overview/classic-prophet-action-branches.tsv and each edition's
complete source/literal/switch material.

Open fields are intentionally typed rather than enumerated as literal text:
the historical-figure language name (or its unknown/unnamed creature forms),
site language name (or unknown site), world language name, the speaker's
generated name and profession/creature caption. The element supplier also
contains grammatical roles 2 and 3; this sentence formatter only requests
roles 0 and 1. Authored names cannot be exhausted as a finite English string
list. This source inventory exhausts the native finite selector/text branches
and preserves those dynamic suppliers without claiming otherwise.
